documents.origin: Bruening et al., PLOS ONE, 2018, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0206162

questions.question: What are the stages of a RAG pipeline?
questions.expected_answer: Ingestion, chunking, embedding, retrieval, and generation.
gold_snippets: A RAG pipeline has five stages

questions.question: How is hit rate at k defined?
questions.expected_answer: The fraction of questions for which at least one gold chunk appears in the top k retrieved chunks.

questions.question: What does faithfulness ask about a generated answer?
questions.expected_answer: Whether every claim in the generated answer is supported by the retrieved context.
gold_snippets: is every claim in the generated answer supported

questions.question: Why does chunk size matter for retrieval?
questions.expected_answer: Too large and the embedding becomes a blurry average hurting precision; too small and the chunk may not contain the full answer hurting recall.
gold_snippets: If a chunk is too large
If a chunk is too small

questions.question: Why can a small fixture not prove the system is accurate?
questions.expected_answer: It only demonstrates the pipeline works end to end; hit rate and recall depend on how gold chunks were chosen, and the LLM judge inherits the judge model's biases.
gold_snippets: A small fixture can only demonstrate

questions.question: How many program jumps were counted correctly by the identification algorithm?
questions.expected_answer: 39 of the 41 program jumps, with one false positive.

questions.question: How many isolated jumps did the skaters perform?
questions.expected_answer: A total of 59 isolated multi-revolution jumps.

questions.question: What errors were found with the peak-to-peak scaling algorithm?
questions.expected_answer: Flight time and jump height errors under 7% and 15% respectively.

questions.question: Where was the jump monitor worn on the body?
questions.expected_answer: It is a waist-mounted inertial measurement unit.

questions.question: What rotation speeds were noted?
questions.expected_answer: Rotation speeds up to 1,500 degrees per second.
